definitions.explanation: Words that indirectly express criticism or displeasure, often through irony or insinuation.
An attitude or behavior that makes others feel uncomfortable.

examples.japanese: {嫌味|いやみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}われて→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦{傷|きず}ついた→傷つく：01934_kizutsuku⟧。
examples.english: I was hurt by a snide remark.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{嫌味|いやみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}われる→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦つらい→辛い：01112_tsurai⟧。
examples.english: It's tough to be on the receiving end of snide remarks from your boss.
They have an unpleasant way of speaking.

examples.japanese: {嫌味|いやみ}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}らないで→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please don't act in such an unpleasant manner.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{嫌味|いやみ}⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦{自慢話|じまんばなし}→自慢話：29001_jimanbanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{好|す}かれている→好く：noentry⟧。
examples.english: That person can brag without being unpleasant about it, so everyone likes them.

notes:
{嫌味|いやみ} covers two related things: a remark that criticises sideways rather than head-on (sense 1), and the disagreeable quality of a person or manner that produces such remarks (sense 2). The sting is in the indirectness — a straight complaint is not {嫌味|いやみ}.

Formation: ⟦{嫌|いや}→嫌：10232_iya⟧ 'unpleasant' + ⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧ 'flavour, quality' — literally an unpleasant aftertaste.

As a na-adjective it describes the person or the manner, not the words:
- {嫌味|いやみ}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a disagreeable person
- {嫌味|いやみ}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{言|い}い{方|かた}→言い方：14165_iikata⟧: a snide way of putting it

Collocations:
- {嫌味|いやみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to make a snide remark
- {嫌味|いやみ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧: to come across as sarcastic
- {嫌味|いやみ}⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧: without being unpleasant about it — common praise for someone who boasts or corrects gracefully

Compare ⟦{皮肉|ひにく}→皮肉：00103_hiniku⟧, which is irony proper: it can be witty, impersonal, or even affectionate. {嫌味|いやみ} is always aimed at someone and always unpleasant.
